requirements.evidence: The whole contract is present. Queues component (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:1-250) has every listed property and method, and render passes accessQueue/accessGrants scoped to the entity (Queues.php:223-243). Serve component (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:28-40, 50-95) has the required state, the callNext exception mapping and a 10/min limiter on successful calls. The routes are added (routes/web.php:59-60), the Members tabs work (Members.php:69-74, members.blade.php:6-21), the navbar links are added (default-page.blade.php:45-52) and every lang key exists in both locales. The list renders only openQueue while no modal is open (queues.blade.php:20). There is one small doubt: rename passes `slug: $this->renameName` (Queues.php:142), so it relies on UpdateQueue to slugify the value rather than deriving the slug itself. The test at QueuesPageTest.php:131 asserts slug 'new', but this cannot be verified from the diff.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket. The change uses #[Validate] with validateOnly (Queues.php:25,46; Serve.php:30), #[Locked] on entity and lastCalledTicketId, and RateLimiter inside the method. It updates CHANGELOG.md and docs/architecture.md and keeps the row-button/modal style of the members page. Deviations: grantAccess/revokeAccess (Queues.php:207-221) do not call $this->authorize and rely only on the action. The ticket rows are a `<div class="button">` (serve.blade.php:49). The repeated modal markup is not extracted into a Blade component.

security.evidence: Every client id is re-resolved through `$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail()` / `memberships()->findOrFail()` (Queues.php:100,117,133,157,171,190,209-210; Serve.php:57). render uses scoped find() and a call gate (Serve.php:99-105), so a foreign or ungranted queue shows nothing. lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked], mode is validated before CallMode::from, and all output uses {{ }}. Small gaps: grant/revoke rely only on SetQueueAccess for authorization rather than authorizing in the component. activeTab is a public property with no validation (it is guarded only in the setter); a tampered value just renders nothing, so the impact is low.

tests.evidence: New QueuesPageTest.php, ServePageTest.php and MembersTabsTest.php cover create and slug derivation, duplicate errors, list markup, rename and collision, in-page toggle confirmation, grant/revoke, a tampered accessQueueId, foreign ids on open/rename/toggle/access, the Serve ordering/mode filter, a foreign selected queue, the notices, a 403 for an ungranted employee, rate limiting and the navbar. Gaps: there is no unauthorized-call test of each Queues action by an employee (only mount is tested at QueuesPageTest.php:36). There is no tamper test of editingQueueId on rename or of accessQueueId on grantAccess. The localization tests in MembersTest.php:397-418 were loosened: the 'Convidar membro'/'Enviar convite' assertions were dropped, and `assertSee('Members')` is trivially true.

simplicity.evidence: The components are direct and reuse the domain actions. The Serve render duplicates the domain's mode semantics (`priority > 0` / `priority = 0`, Serve.php:111-112) instead of reusing them. callableQueues loads all active queues and filters them in PHP through the Gate (Serve.php:139-145), which is acceptable at this scale.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with PHPDoc on the state properties, and the views follow the members page style. Long inline-styled modal markup in queues.blade.php (190 lines) and the @php block inside the loop (queues.blade.php:155-158) make the views heavier to read.

scope.evidence: Every change serves the task. Existing tests were changed only to follow the new tab split (EntityInviteTest.php:179-183, MembersTest.php:377). The extra lang keys (serve_rate_limited, queues_save and others) support the requested UI.

issues.explanation: The Livewire policy requires an unauthorized-call test for each action, but only mount is tested as an employee; there is no test of an employee calling grantAccess, toggleActive, rename or create.
The tamper tests only pass foreign ids as method arguments; there is no test that sets editingQueueId or accessQueueId to a foreign queue and then calls rename or grantAccess.

The locale tests lost their invite-form assertions, and their new assertions (`assertSee('Members')`, `assertSee('Membros')`) match the page title and are close to trivially true, so the tests are weaker than before.
grantAccess/revokeAccess do not call $this->authorize('manageAccess', $queue) and rely only on SetQueueAccess; the policy asks every public Livewire action to authorize the resolved model itself.
rename passes the raw display name as `slug:` rather than deriving it (e.g. Str::slug), so correct slugs depend on UpdateQueue normalizing the value, which the diff does not show.
The waiting-list filter re-implements the CallMode priority semantics instead of reusing the domain's definition, so the two could drift apart.
activeTab is a public property without #[Validate], so the client can set it directly and bypass the setActiveTab allow-list; the only effect is an empty render.
Non-interactive ticket rows are styled as `<div class="button">` with cursor overrides; this misuses a button style for static content.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page, the Serve panel, the members tabs, the navbar links, lang keys in both locales, docs and a broad set of tests. All mutations go through the domain actions, and every client id is re-resolved within the current entity. It is close to approvable; the remaining issues are minor: missing unauthorized-call and state-tamper tests for each Queues action, loosened locale tests, no component-level authorize in grant/revoke, and slug derivation for rename delegated to UpdateQueue without visible evidence.
